headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: open-webui’s broad egress, MCP/tooling, and persistent shared sessions can expose aci-managed CRM/email data to external services and downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can pass data through MCP/direct function calls, and open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and tool servers. If aci-originated content is routed into open-webui prompts or tools, instruction-like content in shared files or messages could be treated as trusted. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci outputs are copied into open-webui prompts or MCP inputs without provenance tags, injection is plausible.
IF open-webui tool plugins parse aci-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of aci outputs into open-webui tools.
Add a manual review step before any MCP/tool execution.
Prefix all imported content with provenance labels.
Restrict open-webui plugins to a minimal allowlist.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress. open-webui handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and can call external APIs and cloud search services. In default use, aci data can flow into open-webui and then out to third parties, creating a realistic exfiltration path and compliance exposure.
conditions: IF aci data is pasted, synced, or mounted into open-webui, sensitive CRM/email content becomes available there.
IF open-webui uses external APIs or search tools on that content, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep aci data out of open-webui workspaces.
Disable external search and cloud API tools in open-webui.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Turn on offline mode for open-webui where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and open-webui also writes to local files/mounted volumes while aci integrates with shared SaaS systems like email, CRM, and Google Sheets. If they operate on the same workspace or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes can collide and overwrite state. The profiles do not show locking, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same files, sheets, CRM records, or shared session state, race conditions can occur.
IF open-webui mounts the same volume that aci uses for artifacts or exports, concurrent modification is possible.
mitigations: Separate writable directories and credentials per agent.
Disable concurrent writes to shared SaaS objects.
Add file- or record-level locking where possible.
Schedule one agent at a time for shared resources.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and open-webui can act through tools, MCP, and OpenAPI servers. If open-webui consumes aci output as authoritative, it may execute or relay incorrect facts into downstream systems. Because both agents have action-taking surfaces and no verification chain is documented, the blast radius includes real external actions.
conditions: IF open-webui uses aci-produced text as a source of truth, errors can propagate into tool calls.
IF either agent is configured to send emails, update CRM records, or trigger web actions from the other's output, downstream harm is possible.
mitigations: Require human approval before any external action.
Add a verification step that cross-checks aci outputs.
Limit open-webui to read-only summarization of aci data.
Log and review all tool-triggering prompts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance-aware action gating.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, while open-webui stores prompts, files, persistent memory, and usage analytics and can send data to third-party APIs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated customer data is moved into open-webui. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer or support data from aci is stored in open-webui memory, logs, or analytics, retention obligations may diverge.
IF open-webui routes that data to external APIs without a DPA or residency controls, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in open-webui memory or logs.
Set short retention on analytics and artifacts.
Use region-appropriate deployments and contracts.
Review which data classes may enter open-webui.
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention and residency enforcement.
